# Merge study (throwaway; generated by run_study.py from pairs/*.json; do not edit by hand)

42 constructed pairs (6 seeds per kind). Experts: 32 hidden units, 16 inputs, 4 classes, trained like the pool trains them. Honest data = fresh samples no expert has seen.

## 1. How often does each test say 'merge'?

Right answers: duplicates MERGE, dominated: retire B yes / retire A no, everything else NO. T5 is directional (retire B in favour of A, retire A in favour of B).

## 5. How the margin trades missed duplicates against wrong merges (directional test T5, one-sided 95 % upper bound)

Each cell: share of pairs for which the upper bound of (the survivor's loss on the retiree's stored samples minus the retiree's own honest loss) is below the margin delta, in nats (0.14 nats is the shipped-style margin 0.10 x ln 4). 'retire B' = A takes over B's samples, 'retire A' = B takes over A's. Wanted: duplicates yes in both directions, dominated: retire B yes and retire A no, distinct no, partial pairs: retiring the expert that knows more is a wrong merge.

## 6. Real experts (the saved operator-by-operator arithmetic pool, 6 experts of 512 hidden units)

6 duplicates (an expert and a shrink-perturbed copy of it, both trained further on different fresh problems of the same operator; 12 directions) and 30 ordered pairs of experts that learned different operators.
